french: Une nouvelle saison s'achève. Il est temps que je m'occupe du réassort du magasin général pour l'hiver...
russian: Ещё один сезон подходит к концу. Пора готовиться к закупкам зимнего ассортимента...
bulgarian: Another season about to end. Time to start working on the General Store's winter restock...

english: Birds are all heading south now that winter is nearly here. It'd be fun to follow them one day, wouldn't it?
french: Les oiseaux migrent tous vers le sud avec l'arrivée de l'hiver. Ce serait sympa de les suivre un jour, non ?
russian: Зима уже на носу, и птицы улетают на юг. Хорошо было бы однажды отправиться вместе с ними, да?
bulgarian: Birds are all heading south now that winter is nearly here. It'd be fun to follow them one day, wouldn't it?

english: The water doesn't tend to freeze over, and thank goodness for that!
french: Heureusement pour nous, les rivières ne gèlent pas dans cette région !
russian: Вода здесь обычно не замерзает — к нашему счастью!
bulgarian: The water doesn't tend to freeze over, and thank goodness for that!

english: Now [Ari], you don't have to say a word. I know what you're worrying about, but there'll still be plenty of fishing here in winter.
french: Ne dis rien, [Ari]. Je sais ce qui te tracasse, mais il y aura encore plein de poissons à pêcher ici, en hiver.
russian: Не нужно ничего говорить, [Ari]. Я знаю, что тебя волнует. Уверяю тебя, зимой тоже можно будет порыбачить.
bulgarian: Now [Ari], you don't have to say a word. I know what you're worrying about, but there'll still be plenty of fishing here in winter.

english: It'd be a big seller, but it's not very practical.
french: Tout le monde se les arracherait, mais ce n'est pas pratique à conserver.
russian: Продавался бы он на ура, но это не очень практично.
bulgarian: It'd be a big seller, but it's not very practical.

english: With summer around the corner, I've been daydreaming ways of getting blocks of ice to Mistria.
french: Avec l'été qui pointe le bout de son nez, je rêve de pouvoir transporter d'immenses blocs de glace à Mistria.
russian: Приближается лето. Меня весь день не отпускает идея организовать доставку блоков льда в Мистрию.
bulgarian: With summer around the corner, I've been daydreaming ways of getting blocks of ice to Mistria.

english: It's tough being a big sister, sometimes!
french: Des fois, c'est fatigant d'être une grande sœur !
russian: Трудно иногда быть старшей сестрой!
bulgarian: It's tough being a big sister, sometimes!

english: Luc won't stop talking about summer being almost here. He's gonna want to go bug hunting every day...
french: Luc ne tient plus en place avec l'arrivée de l'été. Je suis sûre qu'il va aller à la chasse aux insectes tous les jours...
russian: Люк постоянно говорит, что приближается лето. Он тогда каждый день захочет ходить ловить насекомых...
bulgarian: Luc won't stop talking about summer being almost here. He's gonna want to go bug hunting every day...

english: Summer's nearly here. Time to tear the sleeves off another old shirt...
french: C'est bientôt l'été. Je vais pouvoir couper les manches d'une vieille chemise...
russian: Лето уже на носу. Пора отрезать рукава от старой рубашки...
bulgarian: Summer's nearly here. Time to tear the sleeves off another old shirt...

english: I can't wait for summer! The Beach is calling to me.
french: J'ai hâte d'être en été ! Pour pouvoir profiter de la plage.
russian: Жду не дождусь, когда наступит лето! Пляж уже зовёт меня.
bulgarian: I can't wait for summer! The Beach is calling to me.

english: (You get the impression that Dozy is looking forward to summer being over)
french: (Vous avez l'impression que Dozy a hâte que l'été se termine au plus vite.)
russian: (Кажется, Дрёма с нетерпением ждёт, когда закончится лето.)
bulgarian: (You get the impression that Dozy is looking forward to summer being over)

english: I've been meaning to ask Dozy about what that means for him.
french: J'imagine que Dozy va être soulagé, le pauvre.
russian: Я собираюсь спросить у Дрёмы, что это для него значит.
bulgarian: I've been meaning to ask Dozy about what that means for him.

english: The dog days of summer are nearly over...
french: Les grandes chaleurs seront bien terminées...
russian: Летний дремотный зной почти закончился...
bulgarian: The dog days of summer are nearly over...

english: Feels like summer just started, and now it's just about over! When I was Maple's age, summers felt much longer.
french: J'ai l'impression que l'été vient à peine de commencer, alors qu'il s'achève bientôt. Les étés me paraissaient tellement longs quand j'avais l'âge de Maple.
russian: Лето, кажется, только началось, а уже почти закончилось! Когда я была маленькой, как сейчас Мэйпл, лето казалось длиннее.
bulgarian: Feels like summer just started, and now it's just about over! When I was Maple's age, summers felt much longer.

english: It's time to dig out the sweaters, fall is just around the corner!
french: Avec l'arrivée de l'automne, c'est le moment de ressortir les pulls.
russian: Пора доставать свитера: приближается осень!
bulgarian: It's time to dig out the sweaters, fall is just around the corner!

english: Spring is almost here! The sooner this snow is gone, the happier I'll be. The road to the Capital has been trial.
french: C'est bientôt le printemps. Vivement que toute la neige ait fondu ! Le trajet jusqu'à la capitale était un enfer.
russian: Весна почти пришла! Чем быстрее растает снег, тем лучше для меня. Дорога в столицу — сплошная череда препятствий.
bulgarian: Spring is almost here! The sooner this snow is gone, the happier I'll be. The road to the Capital has been trial.

english: I'm going to miss winter. Mom never gets mad when I play in the snow, but she always gets mad when I play in the mud.
french: L'hiver va me manquer. Maman ne me gronde jamais quand je joue dans la neige, mais elle se met en rogne si je joue dans la boue.
russian: Я буду скучать по зиме. Мама никогда не ругается, когда я играю в снегу. А когда играю в грязи, ругается всегда.
bulgarian: I'm going to miss winter. Mom never gets mad when I play in the snow, but she always gets mad when I play in the mud.

english: Now those were REAL winters!
french: À l'époque, c'était vraiment des hivers !
russian: Вот это были НАСТОЯЩИЕ зимы!
bulgarian: Now those were REAL winters!

english: Winter's almost over, and it wasn't too bad. Remind me to tell you about the winters when I was a lad sometime.
french: L'hiver touche à sa fin, il n'a pas été trop rude. Un jour, tu me feras penser à te raconter les hivers quand j'étais enfant.
russian: Зима почти прошла — и прошла неплохо. Напомни мне как-нибудь рассказать тебе, какие зимы бывали в моём детстве.
bulgarian: Winter's almost over, and it wasn't too bad. Remind me to tell you about the winters when I was a lad sometime.

english: Winter is ending, time to start thinking about my spring workout routine!
french: L'hiver se termine. Il est temps que je réfléchisse à mon programme d'entraînement du printemps.
russian: Зима заканчивается, так что пора придумать схему тренировок на весну!
bulgarian: Winter is ending, time to start thinking about my spring workout routine!

english: Good morning!
bulgarian: Good morning!

english: Nice to see another early riser up and about!
bulgarian: Nice to see another early riser up and about!

english: Just smell that fresh morning air!
bulgarian: Just smell that fresh morning air!

english: Another new day, let's make the most of it!
bulgarian: Another new day, let's make the most of it!

english: Ah, another day in Mistria.
bulgarian: Ah, another day in Mistria.

english: Good morning! Hope you slept as well as I did last night.
french: Bonjour ! J'espère que tu as aussi bien dormi que moi la nuit dernière.
russian: Доброе утро! Мне спалось просто замечательно. Надеюсь, тебе тоже.
bulgarian: Good morning! Hope you slept as well as I did last night.

english: It's a fine morning, isn't it? The older I get the more I appreciate them.
french: C'est une belle matinée, hein ? Plus j'avance dans la vie, plus j'apprécie le lever du jour.
russian: Хорошее сегодня утречко! Чем дольше живу, тем больше мне нравится эта пора.
bulgarian: It's a fine morning, isn't it? The older I get the more I appreciate them.

english: You can really feel that winter's on its way in the early morning, huh? Brr!
bulgarian: You can really feel that winter's on its way in the early morning, huh? Brr!

english: Everyone's so... cheery. Like they're about to break into song.
french: Les gens sont tous de bonne humeur. On dirait qu'ils vont se mettre à chanter.
russian: Все такие... жизнерадостные. Как будто вот-вот начнут петь.
bulgarian: Everyone's so... cheery. Like they're about to break into song.

english: Early mornings are my least favorite time in Mistria.
french: Le petit matin, c'est le moment de la journée que j'aime le moins à Mistria.
russian: Раннее утро — моё самое нелюбимое время в Мистрии.
bulgarian: Early mornings are my least favorite time in Mistria.

english: Good morning.
french: Bonjour.
russian: Доброе утро.
bulgarian: Good morning.

english: Morning...
french: Bonjour...
russian: Доброе...
bulgarian: Morning...

english: I'm not sleepy!
french: Non, pas du tout !
russian: Я не соня!
bulgarian: I'm not sleepy!

english: Goooood morning!
french: Bonjouuur !
russian: До-о-оброе утречко!
bulgarian: Goooood morning!

english: Looks like someone's still sleepy!
french: Je connais quelqu'un qui dort encore !
russian: Вижу, кое-кто у нас соня!
bulgarian: Looks like someone's still sleepy!

english: Morning.
french: Bonjour.
russian: Утро.
bulgarian: Morning.

english: It's a great way to get yourself fired up!
french: C'est l'idéal pour être en pleine forme !
russian: По-моему, отличный способ разогреться с утра!
bulgarian: It's a great way to get yourself fired up!

english: Bet it's easy to start your day with some early morning exercise on your farm, right, [Ari]?
french: Dans une ferme, c'est facile de commencer la journée en faisant un peu d'exercice, pas vrai, [Ari] ?
russian: Наверняка тебе на ферме легко начинать день с утренней зарядки, да, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Bet it's easy to start your day with some early morning exercise on your farm, right, [Ari]?

english: And if not, I hope you order one at the Inn!
french: Si ce n'est pas le cas, viens à l'auberge !
russian: А если нет, то заходи позавтракать в трактир!
bulgarian: And if not, I hope you order one at the Inn!

english: Good morning! Hope you've had breakfast, [Ari]!
french: Bonjour ! J'espère que tu as pris ton petit-déjeuner, [Ari].
russian:
Доброе утро! Надеюсь, ты уже

позавтракали

позавтракалапозавтракалпозавтракало, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Good morning! Hope you've had breakfast, [Ari]!

english: Oh, did you just wake up? For one such as I, sleep is more... optional.
french: Oh, tu viens de te réveiller ? Pour moi, le sommeil n'a rien d'obligatoire.
russian:
О, ты только

проснулись

проснуласьпроснулсяпроснулось? Для таких, как я, сон... необязателен.
bulgarian: Oh, did you just wake up? For one such as I, sleep is more... optional.

english: Looks like another scorcher! Best to get anything urgent done in the morning when it's cooler.
bulgarian: Looks like another scorcher! Best to get anything urgent done in the morning when it's cooler.

english: Morning, [Ari]! Let's both find some time to do a little fishing today, eh?
french: Bonjour, [Ari] ! On essaie d'aller pêcher ensemble aujourd'hui, d'accord ?
russian: Утро, [Ari]! Надеюсь, и у меня и у тебя сегодня найдётся минутка порыбачить.
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! Let's both find some time to do a little fishing today, eh?

english: Is there anything better than a winter morning? Mistria feels so fresh and clean!
bulgarian: Is there anything better than a winter morning? Mistria feels so fresh and clean!

english: Good evening!
bulgarian: Good evening!

english: Isn't Mistria peaceful after the sun sets?
bulgarian: Isn't Mistria peaceful after the sun sets?

english: Out for a late night stroll? It's a great way to relax before bed.
bulgarian: Out for a late night stroll? It's a great way to relax before bed.

english: Another full day! Here's hoping you had a good one, [Ari].
bulgarian: Another full day! Here's hoping you had a good one, [Ari].

english: Doubt I'll see you again before bed, so good night [Ari]!
bulgarian: Doubt I'll see you again before bed, so good night [Ari]!

english: I suppose I should think about heading to bed, lots to do tomorrow.
french: Je ferais mieux d'aller me coucher, j'ai beaucoup de travail demain.
russian: Полагаю, пора начинать готовиться ко сну. Завтра предстоит много дел.
bulgarian: I suppose I should think about heading to bed, lots to do tomorrow.

english: I guess I should give it a rest.
french: Je vais dormir dessus.
russian: Что ж, утро вечера мудренее!
bulgarian: I guess I should give it a rest.

english: I've been trying to think of a good sleep pun, but it's getting late.
french: J'essaie de trouver un jeu de mots sur le soir, mais il commence à se faire tard.
russian: Я пытался придумать хорошую шутку про сон, но уже поздно.
bulgarian: I've been trying to think of a good sleep pun, but it's getting late.

english: Look how late it is! Time sure does fly these days.
french: Tu as vu l'heure ? Le temps passe à une vitesse folle en ce moment.
russian: Смотри-ка, уже так темно! Как время-то летит.
bulgarian: Look how late it is! Time sure does fly these days.

english: I don't think the day really starts until the sun sets.
french: Pour moi, la journée commence vraiment quand le soleil se couche.
russian: Я считаю, с заходом солнца день только начинается.
bulgarian: I don't think the day really starts until the sun sets.

english: Ahh.
french: Ah...
bulgarian: Ahh.

english: Nice thing about retiring is you can stay up as late you want!
french: Ce qui est bien à la retraite, c'est qu'on peut se coucher à l'heure qu'on veut.
russian: Хорошо быть пенсионером: можно ложиться спать, когда захочешь!
bulgarian: Nice thing about retiring is you can stay up as late you want!

english: Evening...
french: Bonsoir...
russian: Ночи...
bulgarian: Evening...

english: It's interesting to see how quiet Mistria becomes at night. Those poor human eyes of yours aren't much for night vision, are they?
french: C'est surprenant comme Mistria est paisible à la nuit tombée. Les humains ne sont donc pas nyctalopes, les pauvres ?
russian: Любопытно наблюдать, как в Мистрии ночью становится тихо. Ваши бедные людские глаза едва ли приспособлены видеть в темноте, да?
bulgarian: It's interesting to see how quiet Mistria becomes at night. Those poor human eyes of yours aren't much for night vision, are they?

english: Hope it cools off a bit, now that the sun is down...
bulgarian: Hope it cools off a bit, now that the sun is down...

english: Up a bit late, aren't we? Be sure to let me know if you're having trouble sleeping.
french: Tu ne vas pas te coucher ? Viens me voir si tu as des problèmes d'insomnie.
russian: Не спим в такой час? Если у тебя проблемы со сном, обязательно мне сообщи.
bulgarian: Up a bit late, aren't we? Be sure to let me know if you're having trouble sleeping.

english: Brr! You can really feel that temperature drop now that the sun has set.
bulgarian: Brr! You can really feel that temperature drop now that the sun has set.

english: It's always nice to be out and about. Seeing everyone working so hard really fires me up!
french: C'est toujours agréable de se balader dehors. Ça me regonfle à bloc de voir tout le monde travailler dur !
russian: Прогуляться всегда хорошо. Когда вижу, как все трудятся, вдохновляюсь сама!
bulgarian: It's always nice to be out and about. Seeing everyone working so hard really fires me up!

english: Hello, [Ari]. I won't keep you, we both know that time is money!
french: Salut, [Ari]. Je ne te retiens pas longtemps. On sait bien que le temps, c'est de l'argent !
russian: Привет, [Ari]. Задерживать не буду, мы ведь с тобой знаем: время — деньги.
bulgarian: Hello, [Ari]. I won't keep you, we both know that time is money!

english: There's so much to see around Mistria, isn't there? I don't think I'll ever get tired of it.
french: Il y a tellement de choses à voir à Mistria... Je crois que je ne m'en lasserai jamais.
russian: В Мистрии всегда есть на что посмотреть, правда? Думаю, она никогда мне не надоест.
bulgarian: There's so much to see around Mistria, isn't there? I don't think I'll ever get tired of it.

english: Hey, [Ari]! Enjoying the day?
french: Salut, [Ari]. Ta journée se passe bien ?
russian: Привет, [Ari]! Как твой денёк?
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]! Enjoying the day?

english: Let me guess, you're busy working? It must stink to be a grown up.
french: Laisse-moi deviner, tu travailles là ? Ça a l'air nul d'être adulte.
russian: Дай угадаю: тебе надо работать? Быть взрослым — такая скукотища.
bulgarian: Let me guess, you're busy working? It must stink to be a grown up.

english: Wouldn't it be wonderful if the whole town was a kind of museum?
french: Ce serait merveilleux que la ville devienne un musée à ciel ouvert.
russian: Здорово было бы весь город превратить в музей, да?
bulgarian: Wouldn't it be wonderful if the whole town was a kind of museum?

english: I should talk to Errol about setting up some signs to commemorate all the interesting sights around Mistria.
french: Je vais voir avec Errol si on ne pourrait pas installer des panneaux pour signaler tous les sites intéressants de Mistria.
russian: Мне надо обсудить с Эрролом установку знаков возле всех мистрийских достопримечательностей.
bulgarian: I should talk to Errol about setting up some signs to commemorate all the interesting sights around Mistria.

english: Why hello!
french: Oh, bonjour !
russian: Ну здравствуй!
bulgarian: Why hello!

english: There's always something new to appreciate, if you keep your eyes open.
french: Il y a toujours de quoi s'émerveiller si on ouvre l'œil.
russian: Вокруг всегда есть что-нибудь интересное, надо только смотреть в оба!
bulgarian: There's always something new to appreciate, if you keep your eyes open.

english: Gotta make hay while the sun shines!
french: Il faut toujours profiter du moment présent !
russian: Надо заготовить сено, пока солнце высоко!
bulgarian: Gotta make hay while the sun shines!

english: Another busy day!
french: Encore une journée bien remplie !
russian: Ещё один день, полный забот!
bulgarian: Another busy day!

english: After all, they're hill-areas.
french: Je pourrais me faire terrasser.
russian: Это же... хохмистая местность!
bulgarian: After all, they're hill-areas.

english: It's a great walk out to the Western Ruins... but when I go through the Narrows I just can't stop laughing.
french: J'aime marcher jusqu'aux ruines de l'ouest... mais quand je passe par les Terrasses, j'ai peur pour ma vie.
russian: Мне нравится дорога к Западным руинам... но когда прохожу Ущелье, постоянно начинаю смеяться.
bulgarian: It's a great walk out to the Western Ruins... but when I go through the Narrows I just can't stop laughing.

english: My, [Ari]! You've always got such pep in your step.
french: Ah, [Ari] ! Tu as un tel entrain quand tu marches.
russian: Ну и ну, [Ari]! У тебя всегда такая бодрая походка.
bulgarian: My, [Ari]! You've always got such pep in your step.

english: I suppose small things stimulate small minds.
french: J'imagine que les esprits simples s'arrêtent aux choses simples.
russian: Видимо, простаков и правда нетрудно удивить!
bulgarian: I suppose small things stimulate small minds.

english: Oh ho ho!
french: Oh ho ho ho !
russian: О-хо-хо!
bulgarian: Oh ho ho!

english: I always get comments about how well I walk in high heels on these rustic country byways.
french: On me demande toujours comment je fais pour marcher avec des talons hauts par ici.
russian: Мне часто делают комплименты насчёт того, как я умело хожу на каблуках по этим деревенским закоулкам.
bulgarian: I always get comments about how well I walk in high heels on these rustic country byways.

english: Of course, now I can nap whenever I want. I suppose it balances out.
french: Mais j'ai tout le loisir de faire la sieste quand je veux, alors ça compense.
russian: Зато, конечно, теперь я могу лечь вздремнуть, когда захочется. Так что есть свои плюсы и минусы.
bulgarian: Of course, now I can nap whenever I want. I suppose it balances out.

english: Always see you running about, [Ari]. That energy is one thing I do miss about being young...
french: Je te vois toujours en train de courir partout, [Ari]. Moi, je manque d'énergie avec l'âge...
russian: Ты всегда куда-то бежишь, [Ari]. Единственное, чего мне с годами стало недоставать, — это такой энергичности...
bulgarian: Always see you running about, [Ari]. That energy is one thing I do miss about being young...

english: Seen any cool bugs?
french: Tu as vu de beaux insectes dernièrement ?
russian:
Видели

ВиделаВиделВидело каких-нибудь интересных жуков?
bulgarian: Seen any cool bugs?

english: Princess Maple is out on her daily constitutional, and greets you.
french: La princesse Maple fait sa tournée quotidienne et te salue.
russian: Принцесса Мэйпл совершает утренний променад и желает вам хорошего дня.
bulgarian: Princess Maple is out on her daily constitutional, and greets you.

english: Can't talk, I've got somewhere to be.
french: Je ne peux pas te parler, je dois filer.
russian: Я спешу, не могу говорить.
bulgarian: Can't talk, I've got somewhere to be.

english: Don't be shy about popping into the General Store!
french: N'hésite pas à passer au magasin général !
russian: Не стесняйся, заходи к нам в универмаг!
bulgarian: Don't be shy about popping into the General Store!

english: Also it like, gets you to where you're going. Rad!
french: Et puis, ça te permet d'aller où tu veux. C'est top !
russian: Да ещё и помогает добраться, куда тебе нужно. Просто класс!
bulgarian: Also it like, gets you to where you're going. Rad!

english: Walking is a good way to keep in shape!

bulgarian: No, it is not nervousness I feel...

english: It is exhilaration.
french: Plutôt une certaine exaltation.
bulgarian: It is exhilaration.

english: As do I. But [Ari]...
french: Moi aussi. Mais [Ari]...
bulgarian: As do I. But [Ari]...

english: Even if things do not go smoothly, we will be together.
french: Même si tout ne se passe pas comme prévu, nous serons ensemble.
bulgarian: Even if things do not go smoothly, we will be together.

english: No matter what happens, I will take your hand in mine, and we will join our light...
french: Quoi qu'il advienne, je te prendrai la main et nous unirons nos lumières...
bulgarian: No matter what happens, I will take your hand in mine, and we will join our light...

english: And if chaos comes, we will revel in it together.
french: Et si le chaos se répandait, nous l'affronterions ensemble.
bulgarian: And if chaos comes, we will revel in it together.

english: It is the eve of our ceremony, [Ari].
french: C'est la veille de notre union, [Ari].
bulgarian: It is the eve of our ceremony, [Ari].

english: I'm so distracted that I can barely get any work done.
french: J'ai tellement la tête ailleurs que j'arrive à peine à travailler.
bulgarian: I'm so distracted that I can barely get any work done.

english: Perhaps I can treat wedding planning as a research project...
french: Je devrais peut-être considérer les préparatifs du mariage comme des travaux de recherche...
bulgarian: Perhaps I can treat wedding planning as a research project...

english: Yes! I'll begin compiling notes.
french: Oui ! Je vais commencer à rassembler des notes.
bulgarian: Yes! I'll begin compiling notes.

english: I can't find words to express how excited I am for our wedding...
french: Les mots me manquent pour dire à quel point je suis heureuse de ce mariage...
bulgarian: I can't find words to express how excited I am for our wedding...

english: What color $flowers$ should we have at our ceremony?
french: Que devons-nous choisir comme couleur de $fleurs$ pour la cérémonie ?
bulgarian: What color $flowers$ should we have at our ceremony?

english: Red flowers!
french: Des fleurs rouges !
bulgarian: Red flowers!

english: White flowers!
french: Des fleurs blanches !
bulgarian: White flowers!

english: Lavender flowers!
french: Des fleurs violettes !
bulgarian: Lavender flowers!

english: $Red flowers$? How romantic... the color of both the metaphorical and literal heart.
french: Des $fleurs rouges$ ? C'est si romantique... La couleur du cœur, tant dans la littérature qu'en médecine.
bulgarian: $Red flowers$? How romantic... the color of both the metaphorical and literal heart.

english: A pragmatic choice. I'll make sure Celine knows we've chosen $red$.
french: C'est un choix avisé. Je vais dire à Céline que nous voulons du $rouge$.
bulgarian: A pragmatic choice. I'll make sure Celine knows we've chosen $red$.

english: $White flowers$? How elegant... there's something so classic about it.
french: Des $fleurs blanches$ ? C'est très élégant... Et il y a aussi une touche classique.
bulgarian: $White flowers$? How elegant... there's something so classic about it.

english: A pragmatic choice. I'll make sure Celine knows we've chosen $white$.
french: C'est un choix avisé. Je vais dire à Céline que nous voulons du $blanc$.
bulgarian: A pragmatic choice. I'll make sure Celine knows we've chosen $white$.

english: $Lavender flowers$? What a lovely suggestion...
french: Des $fleurs violettes$ ? Quelle merveilleuse idée !
bulgarian: $Lavender flowers$? What a lovely suggestion...

english: Ah. Did you choose that color because you know I'm partial to it?
french: Ah, as-tu choisi cette couleur parce que tu sais que je l'adore ?
bulgarian: Ah. Did you choose that color because you know I'm partial to it?

english: I'm touched. I'll make sure Celine knows we've chosen $lavender$.
french: Je suis touchée. Je vais dire à Céline que nous voulons des $fleurs violettes$.
bulgarian: I'm touched. I'll make sure Celine knows we've chosen $lavender$.

english: [Ari]! There's an important issue that I can't possibly decide alone...
french: [Ari] ! J'ai absolument besoin de ton avis pour une décision capitale...
bulgarian: [Ari]! There's an important issue that I can't possibly decide alone...

english: What sort of $cake$ should we serve at the reception?
french: Quel genre de $gâteau$ veux-tu servir en dessert ?
bulgarian: What sort of $cake$ should we serve at the reception?

english: Vanilla!
french: Un gâteau à la vanille !
bulgarian: Vanilla!

english: Chocolate!
french: Un gâteau au chocolat !
bulgarian: Chocolate!

english: Rose Hip cake!
french: Un gâteau à l'églantine !
bulgarian: Rose Hip cake!

english: It sounds wonderful. I'll make certain Darcy knows we've decided on =Rose Hip= cake.
french: C'est une merveilleuse idée. Je vais prévenir Darcy que nous avons choisi le gâteau à l'=églantine=.
bulgarian: It sounds wonderful. I'll make certain Darcy knows we've decided on =Rose Hip= cake.

english: $Vanilla Cake$? With buttercream frosting?
french: Un $gâteau à la vanille$ ? Avec un glaçage au beurre ?
bulgarian: $Vanilla Cake$? With buttercream frosting?

english: Yes, that sounds lovely. Traditions exist for a reason, after all... I'm certain everyone will love it.
french: Oui, ça me paraît bien. Les traditions n'existent pas pour rien, après tout... Je suis sûre que ça plaira à tout le monde.
bulgarian: Yes, that sounds lovely. Traditions exist for a reason, after all... I'm certain everyone will love it.

english: Perfect. I'll make certain Darcy knows we've decided on $Vanilla Cake$.
french: Parfait. Je vais prévenir Darcy que nous avons choisi le $gâteau à la vanille$.
bulgarian: Perfect. I'll make certain Darcy knows we've decided on $Vanilla Cake$.

english: $Chocolate Cake$? The type with a ganache coating?
french: Un $gâteau au chocolat$ ? Recouvert d'une sorte de ganache ?
bulgarian: $Chocolate Cake$? The type with a ganache coating?

english: Yes, that's certain to be a crowd-pleaser. I doubt we'll have any leftovers to bring home.
french: Oui, ça devrait faire plaisir au plus grand nombre. À mon avis, il n'en restera pas une miette à la fin de la réception.
bulgarian: Yes, that's certain to be a crowd-pleaser. I doubt we'll have any leftovers to bring home.

english: Perfect. I'll make certain Darcy knows we've decided on $Chocolate Cake$.
french: Parfait. Je vais prévenir Darcy que nous avons choisi le $gâteau au chocolat$.
bulgarian: Perfect. I'll make certain Darcy knows we've decided on $Chocolate Cake$.

english: Oh! =Rose Hip= cake?
french: Oh ! Un gâteau à l'=églantine= ?
bulgarian: Oh! =Rose Hip= cake?

english: How did you know that's one of my very favorite flavors? That type of cake isn't so common here... I haven't had it in ages.
french: Comment sais-tu que c'est un de mes parfums préférés ? Ce n'est pas un gâteau très répandu par ici... Je n'en ai pas mangé depuis des lustres.
bulgarian: How did you know that's one of my very favorite flavors? That type of cake isn't so common here... I haven't had it in ages.

english: [Ari], I have a confession to make. My knowledge of desserts is actually quite poor... I'm in need of your expertise.
french: [Ari], j'ai une confession à te faire. Je n'y connais pas grand-chose en desserts, alors j'ai besoin de ton aide.
bulgarian: [Ari], I have a confession to make. My knowledge of desserts is actually quite poor... I'm in need of your expertise.

english: What sort of $meal$ would you like to serve at the reception?
french: Quel $plat$ aimerais-tu servir à nos convives ?
bulgarian: What sort of $meal$ would you like to serve at the reception?

english: Harvest Plate!
french: Une assiette des récoltes !
bulgarian: Harvest Plate!

english: Mushroom Steak Dinner!
french: Un plat de pleurotes !
bulgarian: Mushroom Steak Dinner!

english: Rosemary Garlic Noodles!
french: Des nouilles à l'ail et au romarin !
bulgarian: Rosemary Garlic Noodles!

english: Wonderful. I'll pass on to Reina that we've selected the =Rosemary Garlic Noodles=.
french: Merveilleux. Je vais dire à Reina que nous servirons des =nouilles à l'ail et au romarin=.
bulgarian: Wonderful. I'll pass on to Reina that we've selected the =Rosemary Garlic Noodles=.

english: Ah, one of my favorites! I enjoy a nice =Harvest Plate=.
french: Ah, c'est un de mes plats préférés ! J'adore l'=assiette des récoltes=.
bulgarian: Ah, one of my favorites! I enjoy a nice =Harvest Plate=.

english: It's festive, and it shows off the best Mistria has to offer. Perfect for a celebration.
french: C'est un plat de fête qui met en valeur ce que Mistria offre de mieux. C'est parfait pour un mariage.
bulgarian: It's festive, and it shows off the best Mistria has to offer. Perfect for a celebration.

english: Wonderful. I'll pass on to Reina that we've selected the =Harvest Plate=.
french: Merveilleux. Je vais dire à Reina que nous servirons une =assiette des récoltes=.
bulgarian: Wonderful. I'll pass on to Reina that we've selected the =Harvest Plate=.

english: $Mushroom Steak Dinner$? Yes, an excellent choice.
french: Un $plat de pleurotes$ ? C'est un excellent choix, oui.
bulgarian: $Mushroom Steak Dinner$? Yes, an excellent choice.

english: It's the kind of dish that's as lovely to look at as it is to eat.
french: C'est le genre de plat aussi agréable à regarder qu'à déguster.
bulgarian: It's the kind of dish that's as lovely to look at as it is to eat.

english: Wonderful. I'll pass on to Reina that we've selected the $Mushroom Steak Dinner$.
french: Merveilleux. Je vais dire à Reina que nous servirons un $plat de pleurotes$.
bulgarian: Wonderful. I'll pass on to Reina that we've selected the $Mushroom Steak Dinner$.

english: Oh! You'd like to serve =Rosemary Garlic Noodles=?
french: Oh ! Tu veux qu'on serve des =nouilles à l'ail et au romarin= ?
bulgarian: Oh! You'd like to serve =Rosemary Garlic Noodles=?

english: It's one of my favorite dishes from childhood... I think it's something everyone can enjoy.
french: C'était l'un de mes plats préférés quand j'étais enfant... Je crois que ça plaira à tout le monde.
bulgarian: It's one of my favorite dishes from childhood... I think it's something everyone can enjoy.

english: There are so many steps to planning a wedding, aren't there? We have another decision to make...
french: Il y a beaucoup de choses à préparer pour un mariage, pas vrai ? D'ailleurs, nous avons un dernier choix à faire...
bulgarian: There are so many steps to planning a wedding, aren't there? We have another decision to make...

english: Everything's in order, and yet... I'm a little nervous.
french: Tout est prêt, et pourtant... j'appréhende un peu.
bulgarian: Everything's in order, and yet... I'm a little nervous.

english: Nervous? Why?
french: Tu appréhendes ? Pourquoi ?
bulgarian: Nervous? Why?

english: Don't worry... it takes two to get married.
french: Ne t'inquiète pas... Moi aussi, je me marie.
bulgarian: Don't worry... it takes two to get married.

english: I suppose it's a matter of circumstance and biology.
french: J'imagine que c'est une réaction corporelle normale.
bulgarian: I suppose it's a matter of circumstance and biology.

english: But telling you what I'm feeling soothes me. Thank you for asking.
french: Mais je me sens déjà soulagée de t'en avoir parlé. Merci de m'avoir posé la question.
bulgarian: But telling you what I'm feeling soothes me. Thank you for asking.

english: Looking at you soothes me too... and tomorrow, you'll be the only thing I see.
french: Te regarder m'aide à me détendre... et demain, je ne verrai que toi.
bulgarian: Looking at you soothes me too... and tomorrow, you'll be the only thing I see.

english: I can't wait.
french: J'ai tellement hâte.
bulgarian: I can't wait.

english: Is that your way of saying you'll be right next to me?
french: Est-ce ta façon de me dire que tu seras là pour m'épauler ?
bulgarian: Is that your way of saying you'll be right next to me?

english: It is... logical. And thus, reassuring.
french: C'est... logique. Et donc, rassurant.
bulgarian: It is... logical. And thus, reassuring.

english: Thank you, [Ari]. You're right. Tomorrow, we'll get married...
french: Merci, [Ari]. Tu as raison. Demain, c'est le grand jour...
bulgarian: Thank you, [Ari]. You're right. Tomorrow, we'll get married...

english: Together.
french: Pour nous deux.
bulgarian: Together.

english: Our wedding is tomorrow...
french: C'est demain que nous nous marions...
bulgarian: Our wedding is tomorrow...
